claims.claim: Fenspiride, a spiro piperidine ether/amine with a scaffold similar to the query's spiro piperidine-tetrahydrofuran, showed absolute oral bioavailability of 90% in healthy volunteers (C01, C02), supporting F >=20%.
Nicotine-d2, a small basic N-methyl amine with low TPSA and no HBD, had 44% oral bioavailability in humans (C13), supporting high F for the similarly small basic amine query.
PF-592379, a small basic amine ether, was predicted to have >60% oral bioavailability with complete absorption (C10), supporting high F.

The high-F records for pethidine and pentazocine were obtained in cirrhosis patients (C06, C14, C04, C11), where first-pass metabolism is reduced; they are not transferable as positive evidence to a healthy-condition query, but they are not low evidence either.
Tacrolimus (~20-25%, C05) is structurally dissimilar and not used as affirmative low evidence.

evidence_gaps: No direct measured oral bioavailability for the query molecule.
No experimental permeability, solubility, or first-pass metabolism data for the query.
Transfer from fenspiride, nicotine, and PF-592379 is qualitative; differences in N-substituent, aromaticity, and heterocycle composition remain.
High ionization at pH 7.4 (basic pKa 9.58, logD -0.37) could reduce passive permeability, but no direct evidence quantifies its impact.
The vinyl group and tertiary amine may be metabolic liabilities, but no first-pass data are available.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high: structurally similar spiro piperidine ether/amine (fenspiride, 90%), small basic amine (nicotine, 44%), and basic amine ether (PF-592379, >60%) support F >=20%; no affirmative low evidence transfers.
